questions.question: Which club has won the most Premier League titles?

questions.question: Which Premier League club plays at Anfield?

questions.question: Which manager has won the most Premier League titles?

questions.question: What trophy is awarded to the Premier League winner?
questions.explanation: The Premier League Trophy (often called the 'sterling' trophy) is awarded to the season's champion.

questions.question: Thierry Henry holds the record for most Premier League goals scored in a single season for Arsenal. How many?

questions.question: Which Premier League club is nicknamed 'The Hornets'?

questions.question: Which player has made the most Premier League appearances?

questions.question: How many clubs compete in the Premier League each season?

questions.question: Which referee has issued the most red cards in Premier League history?

questions.question: Manchester City won four consecutive Premier League titles from which year?

questions.question: Which PL player has the most goal contributions (goals + assists) in a single season?

questions.question: Who scored the winning goal for Manchester City in the dying moments to win the 2011–12 Premier League title?

questions.question: In 2022–23, how many goals did Erling Haaland score in his debut PL season?

questions.question: Which club plays at the Etihad Stadium?

questions.question: What is the nickname given to the match between Arsenal and Tottenham?

questions.question: Which player won the Premier League Golden Boot in the 2019–20 season?

questions.question: Which PL club is associated with the chant 'You'll Never Walk Alone'?
questions.explanation: 'You'll Never Walk Alone' is the anthem of Liverpool FC, sung before every home match.

questions.question: Where was the first FIFA World Cup held?

questions.question: Which nation scored the most goals in a single World Cup tournament (record)?

questions.question: Who scored the 'Hand of God' goal?

questions.question: Which country hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation: Qatar hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup — the first ever held in the Middle East.

questions.question: What is the score of the biggest win in World Cup history?

questions.question: How many countries co-hosted the 2002 World Cup?

questions.question: Who won the 2018 FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation: France defeated Croatia 4-2 in the final of the 2018 Russia World Cup.

questions.question: Who became the first player to score in four World Cups?

questions.question: Which goalkeeper was named best keeper at the 2022 World Cup?

questions.question: In which World Cup did a team score 7 goals against Brazil in the semi-final?

questions.question: What award is given to the World Cup's top scorer?
questions.explanation: The FIFA World Cup Golden Boot is awarded to the tournament's top scorer.

questions.question: Which team lost in the final of three consecutive World Cups (1974, 1978, 1982)?
questions.explanation: The Netherlands lost World Cup finals in 1974 (West Germany), 1978 (Argentina), and then again in 2010 (Spain).

questions.question: Which country lifted the World Cup trophy on home soil?

questions.question: What is Pelé's real full name?

questions.question: How old was Pelé when he won his first World Cup?

questions.question: Which player scored the fastest goal in World Cup history?

questions.question: What year did Argentina last win the World Cup before 2022?
questions.explanation: Argentina won the World Cup in 1986 under Diego Maradona — their second title.

questions.question: Which World Cup mascot became the most globally famous?
questions.explanation: Fuleco, an armadillo mascot, became widely famous at the 2014 Brazil World Cup.

questions.question: Who scored Germany's 7th goal in the 7-1 semi-final win over Brazil in 2014?
questions.explanation: André Schürrle came off the bench to score twice, including Germany's 7th goal.

questions.question: Who was the coach of France when they won the 2018 World Cup?
questions.explanation: Didier Deschamps coached France to World Cup glory in Russia 2018.

questions.question: Which African country became the first to reach the World Cup semi-finals?
questions.explanation: Morocco made history at Qatar 2022 by becoming the first African team to reach the World Cup semi-finals.

questions.question: How many yellow cards does a player need to accumulate before a World Cup to receive a one-match ban?

questions.question: What shape is the FIFA World Cup trophy?
options: Two figures holding up the Earth

questions.question: The Jabulani was the official match ball at which World Cup?

questions.question: Who was the last player to score a hat-trick in a World Cup final?
questions.explanation: Geoff Hurst's 1966 hat-trick vs. West Germany remains the only hat-trick in a World Cup final — Mbappé had 3 but lost.

questions.question: Which country was the runner-up at the 2010 World Cup?
questions.explanation: The Netherlands lost 1-0 to Spain in extra time at the 2010 World Cup final in Johannesburg.

questions.question: What is the traditional colour of Brazil's home football kit?
questions.explanation: Brazil's famous home kit is the iconic yellow jersey with green trim.

questions.question: Which South American country is the only one never to have qualified for a World Cup?

questions.question: Which country hosted the 1998 World Cup?

questions.question: Which Asian team reached the 2002 World Cup semi-finals?
questions.explanation: South Korea reached the semi-finals of the 2002 World Cup co-hosted on home soil.

questions.question: Who is the youngest player ever to play in a World Cup?

questions.question: Which country won the very first World Cup in 1930?
questions.explanation: Uruguay defeated Argentina 4-2 in the 1930 World Cup final held in Montevideo.

Host nations do not need to qualify
Hosts play a playoff to qualify

questions.question: Nigeria's national team is nicknamed what?

questions.question: What country's team is called 'The Indomitable Lions'?

questions.question: Which club does Achraf Hakimi play for in Europe?
questions.explanation: Achraf Hakimi plays for Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and represents Morocco internationally.

questions.question: Ivory Coast's national team is nicknamed what?
questions.explanation: Ivory Coast's football team is known as Les Éléphants (The Elephants).

questions.question: How many AFCON titles has Ivory Coast won?

questions.question: How often is the Africa Cup of Nations held?

questions.question: Which player scored a famous goal from half-way for Ivory Coast at an AFCON tournament?

questions.question: Tunisia's national team is nicknamed what?

questions.question: How many times has Ghana won the AFCON?

questions.question: What is the first move 1.e4 commonly known as?
questions.explanation: 1.e4 is called the King's Pawn Opening — the most common starting move in chess.

questions.question: What opening starts with 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5?
questions.explanation: The Ruy Lopez (Spanish Game) is one of the oldest and most analysed openings in chess.

questions.question: The Sicilian Defense begins with which move by Black?
questions.explanation: 1...c5 is the Sicilian Defense — the most popular response to 1.e4.

questions.question: What is the key idea behind the King's Indian Defense?
options: Fianchetto the kingside bishop and counterattack
Trade pieces early for endgame advantage
questions.answer: Fianchetto the kingside bishop and counterattack
questions.explanation: In the KID, Black fianchettoes with ...g6 and ...Bg7, then launches a kingside counterattack.

questions.question: Which opening starts 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4?
questions.explanation: The Scotch Game was popular in the 19th century and revived by Kasparov in the 1990s.

questions.question: The French Defense starts with 1.e4 and Black responds with?
questions.explanation: 1...e6 is the French Defense — Black will follow with ...d5 to contest the centre.

questions.question: What special move allows a king and rook to swap positions?
questions.explanation: Castling moves the king two squares towards a rook; the rook then moves to the other side of the king.

questions.question: What school of thought controls the centre with pieces rather than pawns?
questions.explanation: Hypermodernism (e.g., Nimzowitsch, Réti) allows the opponent to occupy the centre, then undermines it from the flanks.

questions.question: The Queen's Gambit begins with 1.d4 d5 then?
questions.explanation: The Queen's Gambit (2.c4) offers a pawn to gain central control and space.

questions.question: What is the term for the initial phase of a chess game?
questions.explanation: The opening phase of chess focuses on development, centre control, and king safety.

questions.question: What opening starts with 1.Nf3?
questions.explanation: 1.Nf3 is the Réti Opening — a hypermodern approach leaving the centre flexible.

questions.question: What move begins the Sicilian Najdorf variation?
questions.explanation: The Sicilian Najdorf begins with 1...c5, 2...d6, and 5...a6 — one of the sharpest opening systems.

questions.question: What is the 'poisoned pawn' variation associated with?
questions.explanation: The poisoned pawn variation (6.Bg5 e6 7.f4 Qb6 8.Qd2 Qxb2) is one of the most aggressive in the Sicilian Najdorf.

questions.question: The London System is a favourite solid opening system for which side?
questions.explanation: The London System (1.d4, 2.Nf3, 3.Bf4) is a solid, low-risk system for White.

questions.question: What is the fastest possible checkmate in chess called?
questions.explanation: Fool's mate is checkmate in 2 moves — the fastest possible game ending.

questions.question: Which opening system is characterized by 1.e4 c5 2.c3?
questions.explanation: The Alapin (2.c3) aims to establish a strong pawn center with d4 on the next move without allowing the Sicilian main lines.

questions.question: What is the Caro-Kann Defense's first move by Black?
questions.explanation: The Caro-Kann starts with 1.e4 c6, preparing ...d5 to challenge the centre solidly.

questions.question: What opening does 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 with a fianchettoed bishop characterize?
questions.explanation: 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 with ...Bg7 is the King's Indian Defense — a dynamic counterattacking system.

questions.question: The Nimzo-Indian Defense involves Black pinning White's knight with?
questions.explanation: In the Nimzo-Indian (1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Bb4), Black immediately pins the knight on c3.

questions.question: What opening involves offering a pawn early with the move 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.f4?
